newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore to spend S$20 mln on telecom network.
newsitem.headline: Singapore to spend S$20 mln on telecom network.

text.p: A Singapore consortium will spend S$20 million over the next two years plugging everyone in the country into a multi-media network, officials said on Monday.
The network, connecting televsions and computers in homes, businesses, schools and government departments, would provide a huge variety of activities, the officials said.
These would range from individuals and firms dealing with the government to entertainment on demand, from electronic shopping to video-conferencing.
It will be built by the Singapore One Infrastructure Consortium, a group of companies led by the Telecommunication Authority of Singapore (TAS).

"The consortium aims for an inital rollout of broadband multimedia services direct to the homes, businesses and schools before the end of next year," TAS chairman Teo Ming Kian said at Monday's ceremony to formally launch the consortium.
"For this, it plans to commit S$20 million over the next two years for network development," he said.
Singapore Communications Investments, a TAS subsidiary, will hold a 40 percent equity stake, while Singapore CableVision and Singapore Telecom will each have a 30 percent share.
The project was announced by Communications Minister Mah Bow Tan in June.
